# dog

**dog** is a command-line DNS client, like `dig`.

It has colourful output, understands normal command-line argument syntax, supports the DNS-over-TLS and DNS-over-HTTPS protocols, and can emit JSON.

![A screenshot of dog making a DNS request](dog-screenshot.png)

## Examples

    dog example.net                          Query a domain using default settings
    dog example.net MX                       ...looking up MX records instead
    dog example.net MX @1.1.1.1              ...using a specific nameserver instead
    dog example.net MX @1.1.1.1 -T           ...using TCP rather than UDP
    dog -q example.net -t MX -n 1.1.1.1 -T   As above, but using explicit arguments

## Command-line options

### Query options

    <arguments>              Human-readable host names, nameservers, types, or classes
    -q, --query=HOST         Host name or domain name to query
    -t, --type=TYPE          Type of the DNS record being queried (A, MX, NS...)
    -n, --nameserver=ADDR    Address of the nameserver to send packets to
    --class=CLASS            Network class of the DNS record being queried (IN, CH, HS)

### Sending options

    --edns=SETTING           Whether to OPT in to EDNS (disable, hide, show)
    --txid=NUMBER            Set the transaction ID to a specific value
    -Z=TWEAKS                Set uncommon protocol-level tweaks

### Protocol options

    -U, --udp                Use the DNS protocol over UDP
    -T, --tcp                Use the DNS protocol over TCP
    -S, --tls                Use the DNS-over-TLS protocol
    -H, --https              Use the DNS-over-HTTPS protocol

### Output options

    -1, --short              Short mode: display nothing but the first result
    -J, --json               Display the output as JSON
    --color, --colour=WHEN   When to colourise the output (always, automatic, never)
    --seconds                Do not format durations, display them as seconds
    --time                   Print how long the response took to arrive

## Installation

Binary downloads of dog are available from the releases section on GitHub for 64-bit Windows, macOS, and Linux targets. They contain the compiled executable, the manual page, and shell completions.

Package manager installations may also be available:
- For Arch Linux: `dog` package
- For Homebrew on macOS: `dog` formula  
- For NixOS: `dogdns` package

## Documentation

For detailed documentation on how to use dog, see the manual page or visit: <https://dns.lookup.dog/>

<!-- This is the dog(1) man page, written in Markdown. -->
<!-- To generate the roff version, run `just man`, -->
<!-- and the man page will appear in the ‘target’ directory. -->


NAME
====

dog — a command-line DNS client


SYNOPSIS
========

`dog [options] [domains...]`

**dog** is a command-line DNS client.
It has colourful output, supports the DNS-over-TLS and DNS-over-HTTPS protocols, and can emit JSON.


EXAMPLES
========

`dog example.net`
: Query the `A` record of a domain using default settings

`dog example.net MX`
: ...looking up `MX` records instead

`dog example.net MX @1.1.1.1`
: ...using a specific nameserver instead

`dog example.net MX @1.1.1.1 -T`
: ...using TCP rather than UDP

`dog -q example.net -t MX -n 1.1.1.1 -T`
: As above, but using explicit arguments


QUERY OPTIONS
=============

`-q`, `--query=HOST`
: Host name or domain name to query.

`-t`, `--type=TYPE`
: Type of the DNS record being queried (`A`, `MX`, `NS`...)

`-n`, `--nameserver=ADDR`
: Address of the nameserver to send packets to.

`--class=CLASS`
: Network class of the DNS record being queried (`IN`, `CH`, `HS`)

By default, dog will request A records using the system default resolver. At least one domain name must be passed — dog will not automatically query the root nameservers.

Query options passed in using a command-line option, such as ‘`--query lookup.dog`’ or ‘`--type MX`’, or as plain arguments, such as ‘`lookup.dog`’ or ‘`MX`’. dog will make an intelligent guess as to what plain arguments mean (`MX` is quite clearly a type), which makes it easier to compose ad-hoc queries quickly. If precision is desired, use the long-form options.

If more than one domain, type, nameserver, or class is specified, dog will perform one query for each combination, and display the combined results in a table. For example, passing three type arguments and two domain name arguments will send six requests.

DNS traditionally uses port 53 for both TCP and UDP. To use a resolver with a different port, include the port number after a colon (`:`) in the nameserver address.


SENDING OPTIONS
===============

`--edns=SETTING`
: Whether to opt in to DNS. This can be ‘`disable`’, ‘`hide`’, or ‘`show`’.

`--txid=NUMBER`
: Set the transaction ID to a specific value.

`-Z=TWEAKS`
: Set uncommon protocol-level tweaks.


TRANSPORT OPTIONS
=================

`-U`, `--udp`
: Use the DNS protocol over UDP.

`-T`, `--tcp`
: Use the DNS protocol over TCP.

`-S`, `--tls`
: Use the DNS-over-TLS protocol.

`-H`, `--https`
: Use the DNS-over-HTTPS protocol.

By default, dog will use the UDP protocol, automatically re-sending the request using TCP if the response indicates that the message is too large for UDP. Passing `--udp` will only use UDP and will fail in this case; passing `--tcp` will use TCP by default.

The DNS-over-TLS (DoT) and DNS-over-HTTPS (DoH) protocols are available with the `--tls` and `--https` options. Bear in mind that the system default resolver is unlikely to respond to requests using these protocols.

Note that if a hostname or domain name is given as a nameserver, rather than an IP address, the resolution of that host is performed by the operating system, _not_ by dog.

Unlike the others, the HTTPS transport type requires an entire URL, complete with protocol, domain name, and path.


OUTPUT OPTIONS
==============

`-1`, `--short`
: Short mode: display nothing but the first result.

`-J`, `--json`
: Display the output as JSON.

`--color`, `--colour=WHEN`

# Note: This works for both Windows PowerShell 5.1 and also PowerShell 7 (Core).
# But beware that in Windows PowerShell 5.1, it has issues with completing args if they start with '-'.
# For more information about the bug, see: https://github.com/PowerShell/PowerShell/issues/2912
# In PowerShell 7+, it should work correctly.
Register-ArgumentCompleter -Native -CommandName 'dog' -ScriptBlock {
    param($wordToComplete, $commandAst, $cursorPosition)

    [string]$argsString = $commandAst.ToString()

    # skip the "dog", split the args afterwards as array
    [string[]]$argsArray = $argsString.Split([char[]]@(' ', '=')) | Select-Object -Skip 1
    if ($argsArray -eq $null) { $argsArray = @() }

    # detect if starting a new arg (aka ending with space and asking for a completion)
    [bool]$isNewArg = $cursorPosition -gt $argsString.Length
    if ($isNewArg) {
        # if writing a new arg, add empty arg so that current and previous would be shifted
        $argsArray += ''
    }

    # get current arg (empty if starting new)
    [string]$currentArg = $argsArray[-1]
    if ([string]::IsNullOrEmpty($currentArg)) {
        $currentArg = ''
    }

    # get previous arg
    [string]$previousArg = $argsArray[-2]
    if ([string]::IsNullOrEmpty($previousArg)) {
        $previousArg = ''
    }

    [string[]]$dnsTypeValues = @('A', 'AAAA', 'CAA', 'CNAME', 'HINFO', 'MX', 'NS', 'PTR', 'SOA', 'SRV', 'TXT')

    [string[]]$completions = @()
    [bool]$isOptionValue = $argsString.EndsWith('=')

    # complete option value
    switch -Regex ($previousArg) {
        '^(-q|--query)'       { $isOptionValue = $true }
        '^(-t|--type)'        { $isOptionValue = $true; $completions += $dnsTypeValues }
        '^(-n|--nameserver)'  { $isOptionValue = $true }
        '^(--class)'          { $isOptionValue = $true; $completions += @('IN', 'CH', 'HS') }
        '^(--edns)'           { $isOptionValue = $true; $completions += @('disable', 'hide', 'show') }
        '^(--txid)'           { $isOptionValue = $true }
        '^(-Z)'               { $isOptionValue = $true; $completions += @('aa', 'ad', 'bufsize=', 'cd') }
        '^(--color|--colour)' { $isOptionValue = $true; $completions += @('always', 'automatic', 'never') }
    }

    # detect whether to complete option value
    if ($isOptionValue) {
        if (!$isNewArg) {
            # if using =, complete including the option name and =
            $completions = $completions | ForEach-Object { "$previousArg=$_" }
        }
    } 
    else {
        # if not completing option value, offer DNS type values first
        $completions += $dnsTypeValues

        # complete option name
        [string[]]$allOptions = @(
            '-q', '--query',
            '-t', '--type',
            '-n', '--nameserver',
            '--class',
            '--edns',
            '--txid',
            '-Z',
            '-U', '--udp',
            '-T', '--tcp',
            '-S', '--tls',
            '-H', '--https',
            '-1', '--short',
            '-J', '--json',
            '--color', '--colour',
            '--seconds',
            '--time',
            '-?', '--help',
            '-v', '--version'
        ) | Sort-Object

        $completions += $allOptions
    }

    if ($completions.Count -gt 0) {
        # narrow down completions by like* matching
        return $completions -like "$currentArg*"
    }
}

=====================

dog responds to the following environment variables:

## `DOG_DEBUG`

Set this to any non-empty value to have dog emit debugging information to standard error. For more in-depth output, set this to the exact string ‘`trace`’.


RECORD TYPES
============

dog understands and can interpret the following record types:

`A`
: IPv4 addresses

`AAAA`
: IPv6 addresses

`CAA`
: permitted certificate authorities

`CNAME`
: canonical domain aliases

`HINFO`
: system information and, sometimes, forbidden request explanations

`LOC`
: location information

`MX`
: e-mail server addresses

`NAPTR`
: DDDS rules

`NS`
: domain name servers

`OPT`
: extensions to the DNS protocol

`PTR`
: pointers to canonical names, usually for reverse lookups

`SOA`
: administrative information about zones

`SRV`
: IP addresses with port numbers

`SSHFP`
: SSH key fingerprints

`TLSA`
: TLS certificates, public keys, and hashes

`TXT`
: arbitrary textual information

When a response DNS packet contains a record of one of these known types, dog will display it in a table containing the type name and a human-readable summary of its contents.

Records with a type number that does not map to any known record type will still be displayed. As they cannot be interpreted, their contents will be displayed as a series of numbers instead.

dog also contains a list of record type names that it knows the type number of, but is not able to interpret, such as `IXFR` or `ANY` or `AFSDB`. These are acceptable as command-line arguments, meaning you can send an AFSDB request with ‘`dog AFSDB`’. However, their response contents will still be displayed as numbers. They may be supported in future versions of dog.


PROTOCOL TWEAKS
===============

The `-Z` command-line argument can be used one or more times to set some protocol-level options in the DNS queries that get sent. It accepts the following values:

`aa`
: Sets the `AA` (Authoritative Answers) bit in the query.

`ad`
: Sets the `AD` (Authentic Data) bit in the query.

`bufsize=NUM`
: Sets the UDP payload size field in the OPT field in the query. This has no effect if EDNS is diabled.

`cd`
: Sets the `CD` (Checking Disabled) bit in the query.


EXIT STATUSES
=============

0
: If everything goes OK.

1
: If there was a network, I/O, or TLS error during operation.

2
: If there is no result from the server when running in short mode. This can be any received server error, not just NXDOMAIN.

3
: If there was a problem with the command-line arguments.

4
: If there was a problem obtaining the system nameserver information.

        labels.append(data[off:off+l].decode()); off+=l

    else:

    rflags = 0x8000 | (flags & 0x0100) | 0x0080  # QR + RD + RA

    import importlib.util
    # Default A
    def name_ptr(): return b'\xc0\x0c'
    def rr(name_bytes, rtype, rclass, ttl, rdata):

            answers+=rr(name_ptr(),1,qclass,300,socket.inet_aton('1.2.3.4')); ancount=1
        else:
            ancount=0
    elif mode=="multi":
        # handled in other server
        pass
    resp = struct.pack('>HHHHHH', txid, rflags, qd, ancount, nscount, arcount)
    resp += data[12:off]  # question exactly
    resp += answers+authority+additional
    print("RESP hex:", resp.hex(), flush=True)
    sock.sendto(resp, addr)

while True:

    handle(data,addr)

import socket, struct, subprocess, os, threading, time, sys, json

def encode_name(name):
    if name=="." or name=="":
        return b'\x00'
    out=b''
    for part in name.rstrip('.').split('.'):
        if part:
            out+=bytes([len(part)])+part.encode()
    out+=b'\x00'
    return out

def rr(name, rtype, rclass, ttl, rdata, use_ptr=None):
    # name: string or bytes
    if isinstance(name, str):
        nb=encode_name(name)
    else:
        nb=name
    return nb+struct.pack('>HHIH', rtype, rclass, ttl, len(rdata))+rdata

PTR=b'\xc0\x0c'

def parse_query(data):
    txid, flags, qd, an, ns, ar = struct.unpack('>HHHHHH', data[:12])
    off=12; labels=[]
    start=off
    while off < len(data):
        l=data[off]; off+=1
        if l==0: break
        if l>=0xc0: off+=1; break
        labels.append(data[off:off+l].decode(errors='replace')); off+=l
    qname='.'.join(labels)
    qtype,qclass=struct.unpack('>HH', data[off:off+4]); off+=4
    extra=data[off:]
    return dict(txid=txid, flags=flags, qd=qd, qname=qname, qtype=qtype, qclass=qclass, extra=extra, question_bytes=data[12:off], raw=data)

class Server:
    def __init__(self, handler, port=15353, tcp=False):
        self.handler=handler
        self.port=port
        self.queries=[]
        self.tcp=tcp
        self.sock=None
        self.thread=None
        self.stop_flag=False
    def __enter__(self):
        if self.tcp:
            self.sock=socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_STREAM)
            self.sock.setsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET, socket.SO_REUSEADDR,1)
            self.sock.bind(('127.0.0.1', self.port)); self.sock.listen(5); self.sock.settimeout(0.2)
            self.thread=threading.Thread(target=self._tcp_loop, daemon=True)
        else:
            self.sock=socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_DGRAM)
            self.sock.bind(('127.0.0.1', self.port)); self.sock.settimeout(0.2)
            self.thread=threading.Thread(target=self._udp_loop, daemon=True)
        self.thread.start()
        return self
    def __exit__(self,*a):
        self.stop_flag=True
        try: self.sock.close()
        except: pass
        self.thread.join(timeout=1)
    def _udp_loop(self):
        while not self.stop_flag:
            try:
                data,addr=self.sock.recvfrom(65535)
            except socket.timeout:
                continue
            except OSError:
                break
            q=parse_query(data); self.queries.append(q)
            resp=self.handler(q)
            if resp is not None:
                # resp can be bytes or list of bytes
                if isinstance(resp, list):
                    for r in resp: self.sock.sendto(r, addr)
                else:
                    self.sock.sendto(resp, addr)
    def _tcp_loop(self):
        while not self.stop_flag:
            try:
                conn,addr=self.sock.accept()
            except socket.timeout:
                continue
            except OSError:
                break
            def handle_conn(c=conn):
                try:
                    c.settimeout(2)
                    while True:
                        hdr=c.recv(2)
                        if len(hdr)<2: break
                        ln=struct.unpack('>H', hdr)[0]
                        data=b''
                        while len(data)<ln:
                            chunk=c.recv(ln-len(data))
                            if not chunk: break
                            data+=chunk
                        q=parse_query(data); self.queries.append(q)
                        resp=self.handler(q)
                        if resp is not None:
                            if isinstance(resp,list):
                                for r in resp: c.sendall(struct.pack('>H',len(r))+r)
                            else:
                                c.sendall(struct.pack('>H',len(resp))+resp)
                        else:
                            break
                except Exception as e:
                    print("tcp handler err", e, file=sys.stderr)
                finally:
                    try: c.close()
                    except: pass
            threading.Thread(target=handle_conn, daemon=True).start()

def build_response(q, answers=[], authorities=[], additionals=[], rcode=0, flags_extra=0, qd_override=None, an_flags=None):
    # flags: QR 1, RD copied, RA 1 unless override
    if an_flags is not None:
        rflags=an_flags
    else:
        rflags=0x8000 | (q['flags'] & 0x0100) | 0x0080 | flags_extra | rcode
        # copy opcode?
        rflags |= (q['flags'] & 0x7800)
    qd = q['qd'] if qd_override is None else qd_override
    resp=struct.pack('>HHHHHH', q['txid'], rflags, qd, len(answers), len(authorities), len(additionals))
    if qd:
        resp+=q['question_bytes']
    for section in (answers, authorities, additionals):
        for r in section: resp+=r
    return resp

def run_dog(args, env_extra=None):
    e=dict(os.environ)
    if env_extra: e.update(env_extra)
    p=subprocess.run(["./executable"]+args, capture_output=True, env=e, timeout=10)
    return p

def show(args, p):
    print(f"ARGS={args} EXIT={p.returncode}")
    print("OUT:", p.stdout)
    print("ERR:", p.stderr)

# Use script utility
def run_pty(args):
    # subprocess with pty for stdout
    import os, pty
    master, slave = pty.openpty()
    p=subprocess.Popen(["./executable"]+args, stdout=slave, stderr=slave, stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL, close_fds=True)
    os.close(slave)
    out=b''
    while True:
        try:

            if not data: break
            out+=data
        except OSError:

    p.wait(); os.close(master)
    return p.returncode, out

import socket, threading, subprocess, os, time
# plain TCP server on 15353 capture
srv=socket.socket(); srv.setsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET,socket.SO_REUSEADDR,1); srv.bind(('127.0.0.1',15353)); srv.listen(5); srv.settimeout(5)
conns=[]
def accept():
    try:
        while True:
            c,a=srv.accept(); conns.append(c)
            print("accepted from",a, flush=True)
            c.settimeout(3)
            try:
                data=c.recv(4096)
                print("got bytes len",len(data), data[:200], flush=True)
            except Exception as e:
                print("recv err",e, flush=True)
    except Exception as e:
        print("accept err",e, flush=True)
t=threading.Thread(target=accept,daemon=True); t.start()
for url in ["https://127.0.0.1:15353/dns-query","https://localhost:15353/dns-query","https://dns.google/dns-query"]:
    p=subprocess.run(["./executable","example.net","-n",url,"-H"], capture_output=True, timeout=10)
    print(url, p.returncode, p.stdout, p.stderr)
    time.sleep(0.5)
srv.close()

def read_exact(tls, n):
    d=b''
    while len(d)<n:
        c=tls.recv(n-len(d))
        if not c: break
        d+=c
    return d
def handle(conn, addr):
    try:
        tls=ctx.wrap_socket(conn, server_side=True)
        print("tls ok alpn", tls.selected_alpn_protocol(), flush=True)
        data=b''
        # read until double CRLF and content length
        while b'\r\n\r\n' not in data:
            chunk=tls.recv(65535)
            if not chunk: break
            data+=chunk
        header, _, body = data.partition(b'\r\n\r\n')
        print("HEADER:\n", header.decode(errors='replace'), flush=True)
        headers={}
        lines=header.decode(errors='replace').split('\r\n')
        for ln in lines[1:]:
            if ':' in ln:
                k,v=ln.split(':',1); headers[k.strip().lower()]=v.strip()
        cl=int(headers.get('content-length','0') or 0)
        while len(body)<cl:
            body+=tls.recv(65535)
        print("BODY hex:", body.hex(), flush=True)
        # Determine query
        method=lines[0].split(' ')[0]
        target=lines[0].split(' ')[1] if len(lines[0].split(' '))>1 else ""
        qbytes=None
        if method=='POST':
            qbytes=body
        else:
            parsed=urllib.parse.urlparse(target)
            qs=urllib.parse.parse_qs(parsed.query)
            print("target", target, "qs", qs, flush=True)
            if 'dns' in qs:
                val=qs['dns'][0]
                # pad
                qbytes=base64.urlsafe_b64decode(val + '='*((4-len(val)%4)%4))
        print("qbytes", qbytes.hex() if qbytes else None, flush=True)
        if qbytes:
            q=parse_query(qbytes)
            resp=build_response(q, answers=[rr(b'\xc0\x0c',1,1,300,socket.inet_aton('1.2.3.4'))])
        else:
            resp=b''
        # Determine response mode from /tmp/doh_mode
        try:
            mode=open('/tmp/doh_mode').read().strip()
        except: mode="ok"
        print("mode",mode, flush=True)
        if mode=="ok":
            status=b"HTTP/1.1 200 OK"
            hdrs=[b"Content-Type: application/dns-message", f"Content-Length: {len(resp)}".encode()]
        elif mode=="404":
            status=b"HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found"
            resp=b"not found"; hdrs=[b"Content-Type: text/plain", f"Content-Length: {len(resp)}".encode()]
        elif mode=="200text":
            status=b"HTTP/1.1 200 OK"
            resp=b"hello"; hdrs=[b"Content-Type: text/plain", f"Content-Length: {len(resp)}".encode()]
        elif mode=="badct":

            hdrs=[b"Content-Type: application/x-unknown", f"Content-Length: {len(resp)}".encode()]
        elif mode=="noct":

    r1_name_off=base
    r2_off=base+2+10 # pointer (2) + type/class/ttl/rdlen (10) - rdata 4? wait need include rdata length: record1 total: 2+2+2+4+2+4=16
    r2_off=base+16
    r1=struct.pack('>H',0xc000|r2_off)+struct.pack('>HHIH',1,1,300,4)+socket.inet_aton('1.2.3.4')
    r2=struct.pack('>H',0xc000|r1_name_off)+struct.pack('>HHIH',1,1,300,4)+socket.inet_aton('5.6.7.8')
    return struct.pack('>HHHHHH', q['txid'],0x8180,1,2,0,0)+qbytes+r1+r2

import sys

import struct
def run_raw(builder, desc):
    def h(q): return builder(q)
    with Server(h, port=15381) as srv:
        p=run_dog(["example.net","@127.0.0.1:15381"])
        print(desc, p.returncode, p.stdout, p.stderr)

def resp(q, ans_bytes_list, trailing=b''):
    return struct.pack('>HHHHHH', q['txid'],0x8180,1,len(ans_bytes_list),0,0)+q['question_bytes']+b''.join(ans_bytes_list)+trailing

def rr_raw(name, rtype, rdlen, rdata):
    return name+struct.pack('>HHIH',rtype,1,300,rdlen)+rdata

run_raw(lambda q: resp(q, [rr_raw(PTR,16,3,b'\x05hi')], trailing=b'abcde'), "TXT rdlen3 len5 + trailing")
run_raw(lambda q: resp(q, [rr_raw(PTR,16,3,b'\x05hi')]), "TXT rdlen3 len5 no trailing")
run_raw(lambda q: resp(q, [rr_raw(PTR,2,4,encode_name("ns.example"))], trailing=b'XXXX'), "NS rdlen mismatch smaller? name len? ")

    res='"'

            elif c=='\\': res+='\\\\'
            elif c=='\n': res+='\\n'
            elif c=='\r': res+='\\r'
            elif c=='\t': res+='\\t'
            elif byte < 0x20 or byte==0x7f: res+='\\u{%x}'%byte
            else: res+=c
            i+=1
        else:

class Logger:
    def __init__(self):
        v=os.environ.get("DOG_DEBUG", None)
        if v is None or v=="":
            self.enabled=False; self.trace=False
        elif v=="trace":
            self.enabled=True; self.trace=True
        else:
            self.enabled=True; self.trace=False
    def _log(self, level, color, module, msg):
        if not self.enabled: return
        if level=="TRACE" and not self.trace: return
        # levels: TRACE, DEBUG, INFO, WARN, ERROR all shown when enabled (debug level includes debug+)
        line=f"\x1b[38;5;243m[\x1b[0m{color}{level}\x1b[0m {module}\x1b[38;5;243m]\x1b[0m {msg}\n"

    def info(self, module, msg): self._log("INFO","\x1b[36m",module,msg)
    def warn(self, module, msg): self._log("WARN","\x1b[33m",module,msg)
    def error(self, module, msg): self._log("ERROR","\x1b[31m",module,msg)

    pid=os.getpid()

    rb=os.environ.get("RUST_BACKTRACE", None)
    if rb=="1":

    elif rb=="full":
        hdr+="stack backtrace:\n   0:     0x0 - <unknown>\nnote: Some details are omitted, run with `RUST_BACKTRACE=full` for a verbose backtrace.\n"
    else:
        hdr+="note: run with `RUST_BACKTRACE=1` environment variable to display a backtrace\n"
    try:
        sys.stdout.buffer.flush()
    except Exception: pass
    err_write(hdr)
    try:

    except Exception: pass
    os.abort()

        self.phase=phase; self.message=message

def rust_u16_parse(s):
    # returns int or None
    if s is None or s=="": return None
    t=s
    if t[0]=='+':
        t=t[1:]
        if t=="": return None
    if t=="" : return None
    if not all('0'<=ch<='9' for ch in t): return None
    # remove leading zeros for overflow check? value
    try:
        v=int(t)
    except:
        return None
    if v>65535: return None
    return v

def rust_usize_parse_kind(s):
    # returns (value, error_kind or None)
    if s=="": return (None,"Empty")
    t=s
    if t.startswith('+'): t=t[1:]
    if t=="": return (None,"InvalidDigit")
    if not all('0'<=ch<='9' for ch in t): return (None,"InvalidDigit")
    v=int(t) if len(t)<30 else 10**30
    if v> (2**64-1): # usize 64-bit
        return (None,"PosOverflow")
    return (v,None)

    p=subprocess.run([binpath]+args, capture_output=True, env=e, timeout=10)
    return p

def compare(name, handler_factory, args_list, port=15420):
    # handler_factory: returns handler function
    failures=0
    for args in args_list:
        results=[]
        for binpath in [ORIG, MINE]:
            handler=handler_factory()
            with Server(handler, port=port) as srv:

            print(f"DIFF {name} args={args}")
            print(" orig:", results[0])
            print(" mine:", results[1])
        else:
            print(f"OK {name} {args} -> {results[0][0]} {results[0][1][:80]}")
    return failures

import pty, os, subprocess
def run_pty(bin,args,env_extra=None):
    master, slave = pty.openpty()
    e=dict(os.environ)
    if env_extra:
        for k,v in env_extra.items():
            if v is None: e.pop(k,None)

    p=subprocess.Popen([bin]+args, stdout=slave, stderr=slave, stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL, close_fds=True, env=e)

    out=b''
    while True:
        try:
            data=os.read(master,4096)
            if not data: break
            out+=data
        except OSError: break
    p.wait(); os.close(master)
    return p.returncode,out

Implemented a from-scratch reimplementation of the `dog` DNS client in Python (`dog.py`), with `compile.sh` producing `./executable` (copies `dog.py` and makes it executable).

- Free-argument classification (domain/type/class/nameserver), explicit-option precedence/errors, IDNA/punycode domains, invalid-domain handling

- All interpreted record types (A, AAAA, NS, CNAME, SOA, PTR, HINFO, MX, TXT, LOC, SRV, NAPTR, SSHFP, TLSA, OPENPGPKEY, EUI48/64, URI, CAA, OPT), heard-of/unknown types (incl. the "DNSKEEYE" spelling), JSON/short/text outputs, alignment (byte-width), colours, TTL/duration formatting, rcodes/status lines, `--seconds`/`--time`
- Transports: UDP (4096-byte buffer), TCP, automatic UDP->TCP on TC, DNS-over-TLS and DNS-over-HTTPS (incl. original's URL parsing panic and explicit-port lookup bug, content-length panic at https.rs:89, TLS port panic at tls.rs:41), nameserver resolution emulating Rust `ToSocketAddrs`/libc getaddrinfo via ctypes, `/etc/hosts` hints warnings, `/etc/resolv.conf` system nameserver
- Exit codes 0/1/2/3 (and abort-on-panic with Rust-style panic messages incl. thread PID), `--help`/version exact text (incl. stray `m` in plain version), `DOG_DEBUG` logger output (INFO/DEBUG/TRACE incl. Options pretty-debug, wire traces, "Length is correct/incorrect" warns)

- Panic thread IDs differ per process (inherent); `RUST_BACKTRACE=full` stack frames cannot match original addresses.

- Some rarely-hit TLS handshake error strings (generic OpenSSL alerts beyond certificate-verify, EOF, wrong-version, reset) are mapped approximately from Python `ssl` errors to the Rust/native-tls OpenSSL formats.
- Exotic Unicode IDNA cases (rare UTS-46 bidi/joiner rules, some combining-mark debug escaping) are approximated; common Latin/CJK/Arabic/Hebrew etc. cases were verified.
- TCP/TLS streams with truncated bodies intentionally hang like the original (loop on EOF).

EOF
